title.narrative: Output 2. Assessment of CCA finance supply and demand in Uganda.
- Mapping of FSPs active in CCA finance and assessment of their relevant lending. - Surveys of demand for CCA lending products by small producers and MSMEs.

target.value:
- Mapping of FIs active in CCA finance and assessment of their relevant lending completed.
- Surveys of demand for CCA lending products by small producers and MSMEs completed

actual.value: - Mapping was completed - A study to understand (i) CCA Finance Supply in Uganda, (ii) End-user interest rate costs for CCA-relevant financing products in Uganda, and (iii) Demand for CCA finance products in Uganda commissioned and draft reports on CCA Finance Supply and Interest Rate developed but, CCA Finance Demand report still under preparation.

target.value: Surveys of demand for CCA lending products by small producers and MSMEs completed.

actual.value: - Study report to understand: (i) CCA Finance Supply in Uganda, (ii) end-user interest rate costs for CCA-relevant financing products in Uganda, and (iii) demand for CCA finance products in Uganda completed. - A landscape assessment report on Fintechs and Agritechs also completed and comprises an in-depth segmentation and analysis of the agri- and fintech landscape in the region, and a listing of successful agri- and fintech solutions, highlighting the types of business models and the maturity and size of the operations. - Institutional baseline assessment report on Equity Bank Uganda Limited (EBUL), the host of ARCAFIM operations in Uganda completed in collaboration with EBUL staff in the Kampala Head Office and in the eight ARCAFIM pilot branches.

title.narrative: Output 4. Loan products and lending methodology development

target.value: Dedicated CCA lending products available in FIs in Uganda

actual.value: - A multidisciplinary team led by the Executive Director of public sector and social investments and comprising of managers from Product Development, Risk, Finance, Marketing and Operations Departments assembled at EBUL Kampala Head Office level. - Completed baseline assessment of EBU’s ESG policy and its existing green products - Organized a sensitization workshop on climate change adaptation with EBU staff - Briefed EBU department heads on needs for CCA lending product development - Briefed EBU executive committee, including Managing Director, on the ARCAFIM programme

target.value: Design of dedicated CCA lending products in FIs in Uganda initiated

actual.value: Due diligence process of Equity Bank Group for ARCAFIM conducted in the last quarter of 2022 and, its Uganda subsidiary was heavily involved in the process.

target.value: - CCA Loans Pipeline Developed entailing documenting the cycle for CCA loans to identify and address any workflow glitches, demonstrating readiness for ARCAFIM - Frankfurt School of Management and Finance contracted to offer the Certified Expert in Climate Adaptation Finance (CECAF) course to Equity Bank Uganda and other appropriate Ugandan financial institutions - 2 sensitisation courses to EBUL field staff on climate change and CCA finance organised. - 3-day training sessions for all ARCAFIM field implementers in EB Uganda branches organised once key ARCAFIM legal and financing agreements have been signed. - consultants to support with climate change adaptation finance product development, pipeline development, and monitoring and evaluation for Equity Bank contracted since these are key interfaces between the Uganda pilot and the regional operations of ARCAFIM East Africa.

title.narrative: Output 3. Taxonomy, impact assessment, and monitoring method.
Comprehensive taxonomy developed identifying eligible and viable CCA solutions for commercial financing.

target.value: Taxonomy peer reviewed and agreed with stakeholders

actual.value:
- A draft CCA Taxonomy Framework Note that identifies general investment categories which are justified and eligible for CCA finance end-use by the private sector in the Sub-Saharan African (SSA) food systems completed.
- A Taxonomy Compendium/Report on key studies and analysis on CCA taxonomy with details of eligible CCA investment options for small-scale crop, livestock and aquaculture producers, as well as agribusiness enterprises engaged in inclusive agriculture value chains and food systems developed by FinRes Group. It groups the investment options according to climate risk type and includes recommendations of appropriate, viable combinations of CCA solutions for regions with different climatical conditions.
Initiated drafting of the CCA Taxonomy Framework Note to identify general investment categories which are justified and eligible for CCA finance .

target.value: Finalise work on CCA taxonomy including (a) organising a Consultative Workshop on the developed ARCAFIM taxonomy and present to partner institutions in Uganda the results of the CCA taxonomy development work carried out during the Pilot Project, and (b) continued work with aBi Finance and Government aiming at the development of a national climate change financing taxonomy, covering both the mitigation and adaptation elements of CC financing.

title.narrative: Output 5. Local coordination ensured between local authorities, FSPs and other financing mechanisms promoting rural finance sector inclusion

Mapping of similar initiatives working with FSPs to finance small-holder agriculture.
Stakeholder workshops, coordination and steering committee meetings held per plan.
Joint analysis with aBi Finance on the possible synergies, complementarities and overlaps between aBi Finance’s operations and a possible ARCAFIM project.

actual.value: - Private sector dimensions of GoU’s National Climate Finance Strategy which will provide an encompassing policy framework supported - aBi Finance-IFAD MOU/partnership framework updated -Engagement with key stakeholders including the new leadership of the Danish Embassy, a representative from the Government of Finland conducted. The IFAD team also participated in various meetings and events of the Environment & Climate Change and Private Sector Development Donor Partner Groups for further coordination and promotion of rural finance sector inclusion.
Joint work with aBi and mapping

target.value: - Continued coordination with local authorities, donors, financial institutions, and other financing mechanisms with particular focus on co-operation with aBi Finance. Specifically, the below tasks will be undertaken: (a) Updating presentation by IFAD at a meeting of the Environment & Climate Change Development Partner Group, (b) Additional support provided to the CFU’s work on the private sector dimensions of the National Climate Finance Strategy, (c) Onboarding value chain specialists to support development of an overall green taxonomy, and (d) Conducting financial analysis of investment options.

title.narrative: Output 1. Readily available data on climate change relevant for Agriculture Finance.
1. Mapping of the ecosystem of meteorological service providers. 2. Report on Uganda climate information, risks, and projections relevant for agriculture CCA.

target.value: A thorough agriculture climate adaptation stakeholder mapping in Uganda conducted in partnerships with organizations active in climate change assessment in Uganda and East Africa

actual.value: -A study report mapping Uganda’s climate change risks and adaptation options completed - Climate Information Studies completed in partnership with the IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC) that collaborates with the Uganda National Meteorological Authority (UNMA) in their Agricultural Climate Resilience Enhancement Initiative-program. The studies also indicates that UNMA is supported by USAID Feed the Future to produce various longer-term forecasts for agricultural use or disaster preparedness. Financial and technical assistance is also provided to UNMA by GIZ and UNDP. - The climate studies also identified that Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) in partnership with GIZ/BMZ implemented a programme on Climate Risk Analysis for SSA countries that covered Climate Risk Analysis on coffee and maize value chains in Uganda.

target.value: IFAD in partnership with PIK undertakes another research engagement with the Pilot Project financing to enhance the understanding of climate change impacts on the agricultural sector in Uganda focusing on two more value chains and refining the CRVA scientific methodology. This will aim to lay the groundwork for effective and bankable climate change adaptation strategies, with useful inputs for ARCAFIM but also for any other planned CCA financing initiatives by financial institutions in Uganda.
Mapping of the ecosystem of meteorological service providers completed

actual.value:
Not done. Uganda National Meteorological Agency is the only official provider. A follow-on project may look at private providers.
Registered 75% since the project was right in not doing the mapping, but still could have done more.
